property_text: Identical (cases, outputs, environment) always yield the identical verdict.
title: Execution nondeterminism (verifier is stable)
claim: End-to-end verdicts flip although re-verifying fixed outputs is stable; the solution/execution side varies.
quarantine_reason: Not shown to be a benchmark defect: the flakes are wall-clock-window assertions failing under runner concurrency (INFRA); the earlier 100% failures were an adapter staging bug that is already fixed.

triage.triaged_by: Claude (Sonnet 5.5) for Breakwater maintainers; harness-vs-benchmark triage
triage.policy: every finding is a harness/adapter false positive until proven otherwise (see receipts/quarantine/README.md)
triage.mechanism: the tests are timing based (SIGINT after time.sleep(0.5); `timeout=5` around 3-second tasks). When the runner executes trials concurrently on a shared Docker VM, process start-up plus the 3s task can exceed those windows, producing partial failures of an otherwise correct solution. Re-verifying the same committed state later (verify_only, idle) passed every time.
evidence: the receipt's 10 full runs map onto recorded trials: base-ca8a35 oracle-0/1/2 (6/6 pass; 5 pass + 1 fail; 3 pass + 3 fail) followed by base2-0c7b0f x0..x6 (7 x 6/6 pass) = [pass, fail, fail, pass x7]; the two failing runs were also the slowest (exec 21.7s / 20.6s vs ~17s typical)
oracle-2 log: stdout is 'Task started. x2, Task finished. x2, Cleaned up. x2' (the program behaved correctly) yet `subprocess.TimeoutExpired ... after 5 seconds` - a pure wall-clock miss
other failure shape: test_tasks_cancel_below_max_concurrent got empty stdout, i.e. SIGINT landed before the program printed its first line (0.5s window)

all 14 recorded verify_only runs on the current layout passed (consistent with the receipt's 8/8); all earlier /px/tests-layout runs failed 5/6 because the bare-name fixture `test.py` was not staged in the workdir - an adapter bug fixed by `_workdir_fixtures`
receipt is evidence-only: no replay spec and no witnesses
triage.not_verified: that the official harness on an idle machine never flakes; the benchmark's tight windows may be a real (minor) test fragility, but this receipt does not establish it. Failure rate vs runner concurrency was not measured
triage.needed_to_verify_as_benchmark_property: restore the task dir; run the full reference N>=30 at BW_WORKER_CONCURRENCY=1 on an idle machine vs concurrency=3 and compare failure rates; only a failure at concurrency 1 on an idle host would point at the benchmark
